correctness.rationale: All finite-dimensional Lie subalgebras split into arbitrary subspaces of V or coset lifts of T-invariant X; spectral projections show X splits among distinct eigenspaces. Type-0/type-1 pair conditions reduce to invariant images in V/X, with H(x,z) counting graphs. Two type-one subalgebras permute precisely when the difference coset is zero or lies in one quotient eigenspace; the fibre factor is q^(n-dim(X intersection Y)). Exact formulas follow. For fixed q, uniform Gaussian coefficient bounds and completion of squares give N1/N0=Theta_q(q^((n-S)/2)). An explicit positive fraction of noninvariant hyperplanes and rank-deficient lifts supply the matching lower bound. Full-rank finite subspace experiments and direct invariant-lattice pair sums were replayed. The proof, not extrapolation, establishes arbitrary q and dimensions; no nonsplit or Jordan claims are made.

value.rationale: The subalgebra commutativity degree is a contemporary natural algebraic invariant. The result treats an entire spectral family in all allowed dimensions and sharpens qualitative near-modularity to an exact Gaussian formula and a two-sided exponential order governed by eigenblock pair products. It distinguishes genuinely nonmodular Lie algebras from the typical behavior of two independent subalgebras and is not a scalar-action textbook corollary, arbitrary slice, or known finite table recomputation.
